_readme: THE SHARED DEFINITIONS (DECISIONS.md, W4, 7 October 2026). One file; each page renders a
collapsed "Words on this page" block (PV.wordsOnPage in _shared/picviz.js) listing only the
terms its claims.json declares under glossary.terms, in that order, with any page-specific
sentence it adds under glossary.notes. Each entry: term (the word as a reader meets it),
short (one plain definition, written as a sentence that opens with or names the term, so it
reads the same in the block and quoted alone), long (optional, a second sentence).
A page that declares a term missing here fails verify_consistency.py [glossary]; a declared
term the page never prints, or a block that is missing or differs from this file, fails
tools/disclosure.mjs. A figure drawn from data belongs in a page's notes, where it is bound
to that page's claims, never in a shared definition.

terms.short: QCEW is the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, the federal count of jobs covered by unemployment insurance.
NAICS 326 is the industry code for plastics and rubber products manufacturing.
Withheld (suppressed is the bureau’s own word for it): BLS holds a figure back when so few employers sit behind it that printing it would identify one of them.
terms.long: The jobs in a withheld cell are real; the number is not disclosed, which is not the same as zero.

terms.short: A cell is one figure, for one area in one year in one industry.
An establishment is one physical site, not one company.
A metro area is the federal statistical region built out of whole counties around a city.
Concentration asks how much of the local job base an industry fills next to how much it fills nationally.
terms.long: Above 1.0× is more than the country, below 1.0× is less.

terms.short: Private ownership counts private employers only, leaving out federal, state and local government jobs.
Annual averages are a year’s counts averaged: the twelve monthly counts for jobs, the four quarterly counts for establishments.
PIC-12 is the Polymer Industry Cluster’s twelve Northeast Ohio counties: Ashtabula, Cuyahoga, Geauga, Lake, Lorain, Mahoning, Medina, Portage, Stark, Summit, Trumbull and Wayne.
NAICS 325 is the industry code for chemical manufacturing, which includes resin (3252) and paint and coatings (3255).
QWI is the Census Bureau’s Quarterly Workforce Indicators, which count jobs, hires and separations each quarter.
A hire is a job starting.
A separation is a job ending, quits and layoffs alike.
Churn rate is hires and separations averaged, over jobs at quarter start.
A location quotient is an industry’s share of local jobs divided by its share of the country’s jobs; economists use it to measure concentration.
A pairing is one tracked industry in one county.
An average weekly wage is the wages an industry pays in an area divided by its jobs, per week, so it describes a group, not any one person’s pay.
An obligation is money the government has legally committed to pay.
terms.long: It is a promise on the books, not cash already spent: the cash that actually goes out, the outlay, can follow years later.

terms.short: A prime contract is one signed directly with the government.
The federal fiscal year runs from October to September and is named for the calendar year in which it ends.
The National Employment Matrix is the BLS Employment Projections table of how many people each occupation employs in each industry, for the country as a whole.
O*NET is the Labor Department’s occupational database, which describes each occupation, including the education its workers report it requires.
IPEDS, the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System, is the federal record of the degrees and certificates each college reports conferring.
CIP, the Classification of Instructional Programs, is the federal code a college files each program under; teaching filed under another code is missing from a count by code.
A completion is one degree or certificate a college reports conferring.
The median is the middle value: half the figures sit above it and half below.
A vintage is one published version of a figure, dated the day it was released; each revision adds a vintage.
ALFRED is the archival vintage record behind FRED, the St. Louis Fed’s data service: it keeps every version of a series ever published.
A Tech Hub is a region designated by the US Economic Development Administration under its Regional Technology and Innovation Hubs program.
CPC, the Cooperative Patent Classification, is the international system that files every patent by subject; this site counts class C08, organic macromolecular compounds, as polymer.
A unitid is the federal identifier IPEDS gives each institution record; one school can hold more than one.
A FIPS code is the five-digit federal code for a county: two digits for the state and three for the county.
An endpoint is the web address a dataset is fetched from.
LODES is the Census Bureau’s Origin-Destination Employment Statistics, payroll records that name the home county and the work county of each job.
Match, or cost share, is money partners promise to put in beside an award: promised, not awarded.
A price level here is BEA’s Regional Price Parity for a metro area, where 100 is the US average.
Nominal means as posted or paid, before any adjustment for prices.
PIC-12+2 is the register’s fourteen-county set: all twelve PIC-12 counties, with Columbiana and Tuscarawas added.
OpenAlex is an open index of scholarly works, their authors and the institutions those authors list.
The corresponding author is the author a paper names as its contact; this site credits a paper to the side that holds that author, not the first author.
Collaborative Research is the NSF mechanism that funds one project as separate awards, one per institution.
A producer price index tracks what a whole industry charges at the factory gate, not any one firm’s realized price or its costs.
